_: The railway route as the user drew it, over a screenshot of the city map. Kept in the sketch's own pixel coordinates, with the transform that georeferences them, so the trace stays auditable: if a leg looks wrong on the map, the number to change is the one that was read off the drawing.
_transform: world_x = ox + scale*sx, world_z = oz + scale*sy. Fitted against the road mask's own bounding box (raster px 18..1418 x 18..1311 = world -2122..-22 x -871..1068) and cross-checked on three landmarks: the stadium ring, the west district's central junction and the southern island. Good to about +/-40 m — which is why the generator searches a corridor around this rather than laying track straight down it.
_route: Blue line, clockwise from the north-west corner. A closed loop: the last point joins the first. Two vertices on the west leg (originally [240,500] and [225,455]) were pushed about 45 m out to sea: the drawn line clipped the west district and the fillet cut the corner off the path A* had validated, leaving 36 m of viaduct 6 m from a facade. TRIED AND REVERTED: moving the five southern-peninsula vertices 100 m inland to dodge the 66 m tidal inlet. The inlet does disappear — the shore line is water for 28 of 77 samples across x -200..-660 and the inland line for none — but the ground inland is lower and undulating, so the bore surfaces repeatedly: one 318 m tunnel with a single 66 m gap became five tunnels with four gaps. Do not retry without also flattening the profile through the headland.
_tunnels: Orange line. Where the route is to be bored rather than carried, given as spans along the sketch; the generator forces tunnel between the nearest route points to each end.
_elevated: Spans, in sketch coordinates, where the line is to be carried down the middle of a street on a viaduct rather than kept off the roads. Inside `halfWidthMetres` of the segment the generator inverts the street's price: the carriageway is the corridor and the ground beside it is refused, and the resulting points are flagged `street` so the renderer builds the steel deck, the second track and the paired columns on the footpaths.

elevated.note: the west district's central north-south street, x -1890, 12 m wide, from its southern mouth to where it bends
the same street's north-east bend down to the northern shore, x -1882 to -1827

_islands: The two shapes drawn in pale green: land to be created in the northern water, so the crossing has somewhere to land between spans.

islands.name: kestrel
islands.note: the long western one, under the middle of the northern crossing

islands.name: gannet
islands.note: the small round one to its east

_bores: Spans the drawing forces to be bored, whatever the cover works out at. The classifier decides tunnel-versus-surface from cover alone, which is right almost everywhere and wrong at the end of a headland: T1 stopped where the hill stopped and threw the line straight out onto a viaduct. A span here carries the bore on past that, as a covered way where there is no ground left to bore.

bores.note: T1 south end: carry the bore to the far side of the headland, but stop it inside the solid rock. Pushed out to the tip (66,340) the mouth landed on a knife-edge of land with sea immediately beyond, so the headwall stood on a sliver with hill on one side only. There is no better landing further south either: past the wedge the ground drops to a 10 m rise and then to flat the line runs above, so a mouth there would either break the carve out through 4.5 m of cover or leave a tube standing on an embankment.
the low rise south of the headland: only 4.5 m over the rail, so this is cut and cover rather than a bore — the trench is carved and roofed.
